input.area: ShareButton + QuoteShare — current click handlers, existing transitions/animations, and where to wire GSAP click-feedback (with an opinion on whether to replace the QuoteShare keyframe pop-in)
components: ShareButton (single pill — Web Share API w/ clipboard fallback + 'Copied' confirmation)
QuoteShare (selection-anchored popover toolbar — X / Facebook / Bluesky / Copy quote / Copy link, with per-button 'Copied' flash)
LikeButton (reference: sibling pill that already does GSAP scale-pulse on click — same row, share button should match its language)
lib/gsap.ts (shared GSAP entry — exports gsap, useGSAP, prefersReducedMotion; plugins registered once, SSR-safe)
input.integrationPoints:
Where the GSAP click feedback should hook in:

1) ShareButton.tsx
   - Add `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);` and attach it via `ref={buttonRef}` to the `<button>` at line 56.
   - Import from `@/lib/gsap`: `gsap`, `useGSAP`, `prefersReducedMotion` (never from raw `gsap` — see lib/gsap.ts header comment).
   - Add a `useGSAP(() => {}, { scope: buttonRef })` scope for auto-cleanup, matching LikeButton.
   - Define a local `pulse()` mirroring LikeButton's signature (scale 1 -> 1.15, 0.1s, yoyo, power2.out) so the three pills (Like / Save / Share) read with one consistent language. Call it at the top of `onShare` (before the navigator.share / clipboard branch).
   - Optional refinement: a separate, slightly distinct confirmation flash when the clipboard fallback fires and `setCopied(true)` resolves — e.g. a quick color/scale tween on the icon — but for parity with Like the single scale-pulse on every click is the minimum.

2) QuoteShare.tsx
   - The simplest hook is `onShareClick(target, i, e)` taking the click event and using `e.currentTarget` for the tween target — no per-button ref array needed, and it keeps the toolbar a flat `map`. Call `gsap.fromTo(e.currentTarget, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.12, duration: 0.1, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, ease: 'power2.out' })` at the very top of the handler (guarded by `prefersReducedMotion()`).
   - Update the JSX to `onClick={(e) => void onShareClick(target, i, e)}` at line 217. No scope/useGSAP wrapper is strictly necessary for a one-shot fromTo, but adding `useGSAP(() => {}, { scope: popoverRef })` is consistent with the rest of the codebase and gives cleanup on unmount.
   - Brand-glyph buttons (X / Facebook / Bluesky) close the popover immediately via `dismiss()` after `window.open`, so the tween will be cut off when the popover unmounts — that's fine, the user has already left for the new tab. For Copy / Copy-link the popover persists 1200ms, so the pulse plays in full alongside the existing `.buttonCopied` gold flash and glyph-swap to `CheckGlyph` — they layer well (color transition is CSS, scale is GSAP).

Files a follow-up PR will touch: ShareButton.tsx and QuoteShare.tsx (handlers + ref/useGSAP wiring). No CSS changes required for the click pulse since it's pure transform. lib/gsap.ts is already the canonical import surface.
input.notes:
On whether to also replace the popover pop-in (CSS `@keyframes quoteShareIn`) with a GSAP entrance:

Recommendation: leave the keyframe alone in this change, OR replace it cleanly — do not stack both.

Reasons to leave it as-is
- It's brand new (PR #181), short (140ms), and tied to mount; CSS keyframes are the right tool for one-shot enter animations that don't need imperative control. The site uses CSS animations elsewhere for similar enter flashes (e.g. `.fragmentFlash` in the same file).
- Mixing a CSS `animation` on `.popover` with a GSAP tween on the same element (or its descendants) at mount risks transform-origin / will-change conflicts and clobbered transforms when GSAP also targets `transform: scale()` on buttons.
- The user asked specifically for click feedback on the share affordance — the popover entrance is a separate concern.

Reasons to convert (only if doing it)
- GSAP would give you `prefersReducedMotion()` short-circuiting in one place rather than relying on the browser's CSS-level reduced-motion handling (the current keyframe doesn't honor it — worth checking).
- An imperative `useGSAP` entrance lets the popover also play an exit tween before unmount (currently it just disappears), which is the bigger UX win than the entrance itself.
- It would unify motion idioms across the codebase — every other animated component (CardGrid, ReadingView, ExpandableSection, SiteHeader, BlockedTagsButton, ReadingPrefs, LikeButton, admin layout) already uses `useGSAP`.

If the choice is to convert: delete `animation: quoteShareIn ...` + the `@keyframes quoteShareIn` block from QuoteShare.module.css, add a `useGSAP(() => { gsap.from(popoverRef.current, { opacity: 0, y: 2, scale: 0.98, duration: 0.14, ease: 'power2.out' }) }, { scope: popoverRef, dependencies: [selection?.rect] })` so it re-plays each time a new selection mounts the popover. Then to add the exit animation, refactor mount/unmount to keep the element rendered behind an `isOpen` boolean and tween `opacity/y/scale` back to the from-state before clearing `selection`.

My suggestion for this task: ship the GSAP click pulse on both components first (small, isolated, matches LikeButton). If desired, follow up with a dedicated PR that converts the popover entrance to GSAP and adds an exit tween at the same time — that's a more substantive UX change and should not be hidden inside a 'click feedback' commit.

Misc notes
- ShareButton appears in three pages: app/chapter/[id]/page.tsx (line 225), app/story/[id]/page.tsx (line 174), app/series/[id]/page.tsx (line 158). The change is local to the component — no caller updates needed.
- QuoteShare is mounted once from components/ReadingView.tsx (line 238); also local.
- app/globals.css line 613 has a `[class*='ShareButton']` selector — worth a glance before changing the module-scoped class names, but adding a ref/handler doesn't affect that.
- Always import GSAP via `@/lib/gsap` (per the lib's own header comment) — never from `gsap` directly.
- `useGSAP` from `@gsap/react` is re-exported from lib/gsap.ts and is the standard scope wrapper across the codebase.
